summary: MPEG-2 Transport Streams are widely sent over RTP in IPTV systems. This document defines an RTCP Extended Report block for reporting decodability statistics for MPEG-2 TS. The metrics do not depend on the Program Specific Information carried in the stream.

eli5.summary: This is a report about whether TV stream pieces arrive in a form the receiver can understand.

subtitle: An RTCP report block that counts MPEG-2 Transport Stream errors so IPTV operators can spot decoding problems.

tldr.problem: MPEG-2 Transport Streams are widely sent over RTP in IPTV systems, but standard RTCP does not tell an operator whether the stream inside is well formed enough to be decoded.
tldr.mechanism: A new RTCP Extended Report block, type 22, carries counts of error events defined by ETSI TR 101 290 (sync loss, sync byte, continuity, transport and clock-related errors) over a range of RTP sequence numbers. The counts do not depend on Program Specific Information in the stream.
tldr.outcome: An endpoint can report bitstream packetization and encoding problems that may affect how users perceive a video service. The RFC is a Proposed Standard with no replacement listed.

today: RFC 6990 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2013, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Decodability Metrics for MPEG-2 over RTP
sections.content:
An MPEG-2 Transport Stream (TS) is a standard container format for multimedia data, and unicast or multicast MPEG-2 TS over RTP is widely deployed in IPTV systems. RFC 6990 defines a new RTCP Extended Report (XR) block, built on RFC 3611 and RFC 3550, for reporting decodability statistics.

ETSI has defined syntax and information consistency tests for monitoring MPEG-2 Transport Streams, grouped by priority: first priority (necessary for decodability), second priority (continuous or periodic monitoring) and third priority (application-dependent monitoring). This block reports the number of occurrences of each PSI-independent indicator in the first and second priorities. Third priority indicators are not supported.

The counts are useful for finding bitstream packetization and transport stream encoding problems that may affect the user's perception of a video service delivered over RTP. The block follows the guidance of RFC 6390 and RFC 6792.
sections.eli5: TV shows travel over the network as a stream of small packets. This report lets the receiver count the kinds of mistakes in that stream so the TV company can find out why viewers might see glitches.

sections.title: What the Block Measures
sections.content:
The ETSI document generally defines metrics for error events, and this RFC carries counts of them, measured at the receiving end of the RTP stream. They fall into two groups. The basic monitoring parameters necessary to ensure the TS can be decoded are Transport Stream synchronization losses, sync byte errors and continuity count errors. The continuous monitoring parameters necessary for continuous decoding are transport errors, Program Clock Reference (PCR) errors, PCR repetition errors, PCR discontinuity indicator errors, PCR accuracy errors and Presentation Time Stamp (PTS) errors.

Other ETSI parameters are ignored because they do not apply to all MPEG-2 implementations. When a report spans more than one measurement interval (RFC 6776), a count may reflect a problem in the current or the previous interval.
sections.eli5: The tally sheet has a row for each kind of mistake, such as pieces in the wrong order or a clock signal that came too late.

sections.title: The Block Layout
sections.content:
The block starts with BT=22, an 8-bit Reserved field and a 16-bit Block Length. The Block Length is the constant 11, and the block MUST be discarded if it has a different value. Reserved bits MUST be zero when sent and ignored on receipt.

Next come the SSRC of the source, and the 16-bit begin_seq and end_seq fields, the RTP sequence numbers at the start and end of the measurement period, as defined in RFC 3611. Then follow nine 32-bit counters, each counting events within that sequence number interval: TS_sync_loss_count, Sync_byte_error_count, Continuity_count_error_count, Transport_error_count, PCR_error_count, PCR_repetition_error_count, PCR_discontinuity_indicator_error_count, PCR_accuracy_error_count and PTS_error_count.
sections.eli5: The report starts with who it is about and which packets it covers, then lists each tally as a big number.

sections.title: What Counts as an Error
sections.content:
Each counter follows an ETSI definition:

  • TS sync loss: two or more consecutive incorrect sync bytes.
  • Sync byte error: the sync byte of a TS packet is not 0x47.
  • Continuity count error: incorrect packet order, a packet occurring more than twice, or a lost packet.
  • Transport error: an erroneous TS packet that cannot be corrected.
  • PCR error: the program clock reference is not seen for more than 100 ms. The interval between two consecutive PCR values should be no more than 40 ms.
  • PCR repetition error: the interval between two consecutive PCR values is more than 40 ms.
  • PCR discontinuity indicator error: the interval between two consecutive PCR values is more than 100 ms.
  • PCR accuracy error: PCR accuracy of the selected program is outside the range of +/-500 ns.
  • PTS error: PTS repetition is more than 700 ms. The PTS aids the decoder in presenting the program on time, at the correct speed, and synchronized.
sections.eli5: Each mistake has a rule, such as the clock signal being late by more than a set number of milliseconds. Every time the rule is broken, the counter goes up by one.

sections.title: SDP Signaling and IANA
sections.content:
RFC 3611 defines using the Session Description Protocol (RFC 4566) to signal use of XR blocks, but XR blocks MAY be used without prior signaling. This RFC adds an xr-format value for the rtcp-xr attribute, ts-psi-indep-decodability, and offer/answer follows the unilateral parameter rules of RFC 3611.

IANA assigns block type 22 in the RTCP XR Block Type Registry to this block, and registers the new SDP parameter in the RTCP XR SDP Parameters Registry.
sections.eli5: Programs can announce in their setup message that they will send this report, using its special name. The report also gets its own number, 22.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Reported error counters may be related to contractual Service Level Agreements (SLAs). An attack, such as RTP endpoints reporting false data or an on-path attacker modifying reported data, might deliberately corrupt the counters, with financial implications for the network operator, either through unneeded performance metrics or penalty charges for SLA failure.

The suggested defense is authentication and integrity protection for the XR block, which can be done with the RTP profile combining Secure RTP (RFC 3711) and the Audio-Visual Profile with Feedback into Secure AVPF (RFC 5124). Otherwise the block adds no new security considerations beyond RFC 3611.
sections.eli5: If someone changed the tallies, a company might be blamed or charged unfairly. Locking the reports so nobody can tamper with them prevents this.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Zero when sent, ignored on receipt.

fields.name: SSRC of Source
fields.desc: As defined in Section 4.1 of RFC 3611.

fields.name: begin_seq
fields.desc: RTP sequence number at the start of the measurement period.

fields.name: end_seq
fields.desc: RTP sequence number at the end of the measurement period.

fields.name: TS_sync_loss_count
fields.desc: Two or more consecutive incorrect sync bytes.

fields.name: Continuity_count_error_count
fields.desc: Wrong order, repeated more than twice, or lost packet.

fields.name: Transport_error_count
fields.desc: Erroneous TS packet that cannot be corrected.

fields.name: PCR_error_count
fields.desc: PCR not seen for more than 100 ms.

fields.name: PCR_repetition_error_count
fields.desc: Interval between PCR values more than 40 ms.

fields.name: PCR_discontinuity_indicator_error_count
fields.desc: Interval between PCR values more than 100 ms.
